read_from: The route text as served: field 1 (the route text) of each row of reader/data/route-store of the main branch at commit 306f3b285898, store_version 87b13b1169b4 (its index.json), for "Unabridged Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew Lexicon structured source" (M46): 8,927 routes (axis: routes), 3,681 letters keys (axis: keys). The definition field of the same row equals the route text on 8,927 routes and the store's cut flag stands on 0 routes (axis: routes). The source's own key to its signs: none found. The lane's record of the source (the dictionary store's records/M46.jsonl, 4,828 records from the file unabridged-BDB-Hebrew-lexicon.csv) holds one marked-up text per entry; its tags show the structure only: the entry's main gloss (highlightword), its marked glosses and translations of verse phrases (highlight), Hebrew (bdbheb), references (ref) and shortened names (lookup, which calls a table of abbreviations that the record does not hold), so a shape that says what one of the source's own signs means begins "unverified:", unless the record's own use of the sign explains it and the meaning says so. The route text names neither the entry nor the tag it came from; the lane read both from the record by audit, which is evidence about the source and no part of any test. By the audit (axis: routes): 4,282 routes are a whole main gloss, 2,290 a whole marked stretch, 361 a part of one of these, 1,942 a stretch of the entry's text outside those tags, and 49 could not be placed.

definitions.terms: In every test: a letter is any character of Unicode category L (JavaScript \p{L}); a digit is any character of Unicode category N (JavaScript \p{N}, as the template's isMark reads it); whitespace is what JavaScript's \s matches; an uppercase letter is \p{Lu}; a letter of the Greek script is \p{Script=Greek}; a hyphen is U+002D only, since U+2010 has its own shape; an apostrophe is U+0027; to trim is what JavaScript's String.trim does. Every match against a list is exact and case-sensitive, each entry as it is written. To begin with an entry is a plain prefix: no word end is needed after it. What a bracket holds, the container, and the text before and after a mark are the template's c.group, c.container, c.before and c.after.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file, and the first whose test holds names the occurrence; so each test speaks only of occurrences that no shape above it, for the same mark, has taken.
definitions.list_text: The steps, in order: (1) trim the text. (2) If it now ends in a period, remove that one period and trim again. (3) Take the first word of the result (see word); if that word is one of capitalised_openers, make the first character of the result lowercase. The result is the list_text.
definitions.pieces: Cut list_text at every comma and trim each part; a part left empty stays as an empty piece. The pieces keep their order; the first piece is the part before the first comma. Every test on pieces stands below comma.in_text_with_other_signs, so no bracket is left in such a text and every comma of it stands at top level.
definitions.other_sign: A character of list_text that is not a letter, a digit or whitespace and is none of these: a comma; a hyphen or an apostrophe that has a letter directly before it and a letter directly after it.
definitions.word: A word is a maximal run of characters that are neither whitespace nor a comma. The first word of a text or of a piece is the characters before its first whitespace or comma, which is empty if it opens with one. A piece is one word when it holds no whitespace and is not empty.
definitions.marked_cuts_rule: Each entry of marked_cuts, small_verb_marked_cuts and small_verb_ed_marked_cuts is one route's text, exact to the character and with nothing trimmed, with the three characters space, pipe, space written directly before each mark the branch may cut. An occurrence stands at a mark of a list when the whole text, untrimmed, is equal to an entry of that list once that entry's ' | ' are taken out, and in that entry a ' | ' stands directly before this occurrence: the occurrence's index in the text equals the index of that ' | ' in the entry less three for each ' | ' before it. A route's other marks do not stand at a mark.

shapes.means: A comma in a text whose brackets do not balance, whether the store's route was cut off inside one of the source's brackets or the source's own text leaves one open, so nothing there may divide.
shapes.test: Every comma of a text for which the ask's helper unbalanced(text) is true.

shapes.means: Inside round brackets, separates the Greek words or spellings of a name that the source quotes.
shapes.test: (The order of the tests is first_match; the words letter, digit, whitespace, hyphen and trim are as in terms.) The comma's container is paren and the text of the innermost bracket it sits in (the template's c.inner) holds a letter of the Greek script.

shapes.means: Inside round brackets, follows a space and lists the source's citations: at about five in ten the record shows a Hebrew word that the store removed just before the comma; the rest stand after a sign or a figure, or in a place the search of the record did not find.
shapes.test: The comma's container is paren and the character directly before the comma is whitespace.

shapes.means: A general shape for a comma inside the source's round-bracket aside: in a sentence or a list of remarks about the word, about six in ten; between two short words that qualify the gloss, as in wide, lofty, about four in ten.
shapes.test: Any other comma whose container is paren, not caught above.

shapes.means: Inside square brackets, separates the parts of a remark or a supplied wording that the source keeps apart from the gloss.
shapes.test: Every comma whose container is bracket.

shapes.means: Separates two readings in a text that a shape below would keep whole, one beside a sign, a tail, a label or a qualifying piece, or one with a capital, a connective or a leaning part, at a comma the ledger read and marks by hand in a closed list; a tail stays with the last piece before it even when it speaks of every piece, and a label at the head stays with the first piece after it.
shapes.test: The comma's container is top and it stands at a mark of marked_cuts: the whole text is equal to an entry of marked_cuts once that entry's ' | ' are taken out, and in that entry a ' | ' stands directly before this comma (see marked_cuts_rule).

shapes.means: Separates the pieces of a list that opens with a small verb, at a comma the ledger read and marks by hand in a closed list: a later piece may lean on the opening verb, as busied with does in be occupied, busied with, or stand alone, as have compassion does in be sorry, moved to pity, have compassion.
shapes.test: The comma's container is top and it stands at a mark of small_verb_marked_cuts: the whole text is equal to an entry of small_verb_marked_cuts once that entry's ' | ' are taken out, and in that entry a ' | ' stands directly before this comma (see marked_cuts_rule).

shapes.means: Separates a phrase from a later word in ed that leans on the opening verb, at a comma the ledger read and marks by hand in a closed list, in a list that holds another sign, as in be out of humour, vexed.

shapes.means: unverified: read here as the source's sign that sets one view against another, as it does beside what other scholars read; in this route it stands directly before the view so offered.
shapes.test: A closing angle bracket for which the template's c.group is the empty string.

shapes.means: Joins two figures, a range of years or of chapters that the source cites.
shapes.test: A hyphen with a digit directly before it and a digit directly after it.

shapes.means: Ends a word part that a later word or a bracket completes, as in ball-, knob-shaped or treading- or stepping-place.
shapes.test: A hyphen with a letter directly before it and no letter directly after it.

shapes.means: Opens a word part that takes the first half of the word before it, as in sheep-raiser, -dealer.
shapes.test: A hyphen with no letter directly before it and a letter directly after it.

shapes.means: A general shape for a hyphen between two letters: it joins a compound word such as fire-brand, nearly all; it breaks a word at a line end or between syllables of a foreign word, as in con-tinuance, a few.
shapes.test: A hyphen with a letter directly before it and a letter directly after it.

shapes.means: A hyphen standing alone beside a space or bracket, a Greek ending that the source writes apart from its word.
shapes.test: Any other hyphen, not caught above.

shapes.means: The Unicode hyphen after a Greek letter, the prefix that the source cites beside the Greek word it compares.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the U+2010 HYPHEN character.

shapes.means: unverified: stands for a Hebrew or Aramaic letter in a name or term that the source spells in Latin letters.
shapes.test: An apostrophe whose whole word (the maximal run of characters that are neither whitespace nor a comma, around it) is one of transliterated_words.

shapes.means: The possessive ending left behind when the store removed the Hebrew word before it, as the record shows wherever the search found the place.
shapes.test: An apostrophe with nothing or whitespace directly before it, and directly after it the lowercase letter s with no letter directly after that s.

shapes.means: The possessive of an English noun, name or pronoun in the source's description, as in David's heroes or one's fill.
shapes.test: An apostrophe with a letter directly before it and, directly after it, the lowercase letter s with no letter directly after that s.

shapes.means: Opens or closes a word or phrase the source sets in quotes: a title or a loose use, as in 'son' of Cush, about seven in ten; an exact term or phrase, as in 'tabernacle' or 'Red Sea', about three in ten.
shapes.test: An apostrophe that either has nothing, whitespace or an opening round bracket directly before it and a letter directly after it, or has an apostrophe of that same form somewhere earlier in the text, whichever shape took that earlier apostrophe.

shapes.means: The possessive of a plural or of a name ending in s, as in Moses' wife.
shapes.test: Any other apostrophe, not caught above.

shapes.means: A colon in a text whose brackets do not balance, whether the store's route was cut off inside one of the source's brackets or the source's own text leaves one open, so nothing there may divide.
shapes.test: Every colon of a text for which the ask's helper unbalanced(text) is true.

shapes.means: Stands before a rendering where the source writes a colon after a sense or a heading, at a colon the ledger read and marks by hand, as in edge: shore.
shapes.test: The colon's container is top and it stands at a mark of marked_cuts: the whole text is equal to an entry of marked_cuts once that entry's ' | ' are taken out, and in that entry a ' | ' stands directly before this colon (see marked_cuts_rule).

shapes.means: Stands inside a reference with no space after it, between a work and its number, a chapter and its verse, or a page and what stands on it.
shapes.test: A colon with a letter or digit directly after it.

shapes.means: Ends a sense's heading and opens the source's outline of its branches, the a. and b. that follow.
shapes.test: A colon where the text after it is: optional whitespace, optionally an em dash (U+2014) and optional whitespace, then one of outline_letters, then a period, then whitespace or the end of the text.

shapes.means: Ends a Greek spelling of a name and opens what the source says of the person or place.
shapes.test: A colon where the last whitespace-free run before it (whitespace may stand between) holds a letter of the Greek script.

shapes.means: A general shape for any other colon: it ends a heading or a label and opens an example, a grammar word or a use of the word, about seven in ten; it stands in a long remark or a reference, about three in ten.
shapes.test: Any other colon, not caught above.

shapes.means: States the sum of two numbers in the source's table of number words, a count and no rendering.
shapes.test: An equals sign where the last character before it that is not whitespace and the next character after it that is not whitespace are both digits.

shapes.means: A general shape for any other equals sign: it restates the word before it in other words, as in take = capture, about seven in ten; it opens an equivalent at the head of a text or a bracket, about three in ten.
shapes.test: Any other equals sign, not caught above.

shapes.means: unverified: opens the source's note on the forms or the list of uses after a gloss or a heading, the forms an entry goes on to cite.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the em dash (U+2014).

shapes.means: unverified: read here as the source's shortened and, joining two names, two words or two items of one description or remark.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the ampersand.

shapes.means: Adds a number in the source's table of number words, a count and no rendering; a figure follows it, and at about eight in ten a figure stands directly before it too.
shapes.test: A plus sign where the next character after it that is not whitespace is a digit.

shapes.means: unverified: says that the word is used with another word that follows, as in + person or + other number, read here as a usage note of the source.
shapes.test: Any other plus sign, not caught above.

shapes.means: Stands after one cry and before another, as in lo! behold!, where two renderings of one word have no other sign between them; a label before the first cry stays with it.
shapes.test: The exclamation mark's container is top; the text, trimmed, is exactly one of two_cries_texts; and more than whitespace follows it in the text.

shapes.means: Marks a rendering as a cry or stands in the source's remark as a sign of surprise, as in how much more!
shapes.test: Any other exclamation mark, not caught above.

shapes.means: A question mark in a text whose brackets do not balance, whether the store's route was cut off inside one of the source's brackets or the source's own text leaves one open, so nothing there may divide.
shapes.test: Every question mark of a text for which the ask's helper unbalanced(text) is true.

shapes.means: Stands after one rendering that is itself a question and before the next rendering, as in what? how? aught, with no other sign between them.
shapes.test: The question mark's container is top; the text, trimmed, is exactly one of two_questions_texts; and more than whitespace follows it in the text.

shapes.means: Ends a rendering that is itself a question, as in where ? or how ?
shapes.test: After removing whitespace from the end of the text before the question mark, the maximal run of letters and digits at its end is one of interrogative_words.

shapes.means: unverified: read here as the source's sign of doubt on the word, the place or the identification beside it, so that a word it follows is held doubtful even where another rendering comes after it, as in thorn? barb?
shapes.test: Any other question mark, not caught above.

shapes.means: unverified: one stroke of the source's double stroke, read here as its sign for a parallel passage or word.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the pipe character.

shapes.means: Stands for the Hebrew letter ayin in a Latin spelling of a stem or a name, as in Niph`al and Se`îr, as those stems and names show.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the grave accent.

shapes.means: Opens a tag of the source's file that names a cited place: in these routes GKC, a colon and a number, followed by the section sign and the same number, a paragraph of a Hebrew grammar.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the U+00AB character.

shapes.means: Closes a tag of the source's file that names a cited place: in these routes GKC, a colon and a number, followed by the section sign and the same number, a paragraph of a Hebrew grammar.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the U+00BB character.

shapes.means: unverified: read here as standing before the number of a paragraph in a Hebrew grammar that the source cites, about eight in ten; inside a cited word, as in daru§, it stands for a lost letter, about two in ten.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the U+00A7 character.

shapes.means: In a cited word, the file's stand-in for capital Ḳ, as its own use shows: about seven in ten of the sign's uses in the record stand under a headword with qoph. Outside these routes the record also has one true dagger, before a year.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the U+2020 character.

shapes.means: In a cited word, the file's stand-in for small ḳ, as its own use shows: about eight in ten of the sign's uses in the record stand under a headword with qoph.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the U+2021 character.

shapes.means: unverified: read here as the root sign, which stands where the source speaks of the root of the word.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the U+221A character.

shapes.means: unverified: stands between two figures in a measure, read here as the source's sign for by.
shapes.test: An asterisk with a digit directly before it and a digit directly after it.

shapes.means: unverified: stands before a cited name in another language, read here as the source's sign for a form it reconstructs.
shapes.test: Any other asterisk, not caught above.

shapes.means: Joins the names of Bible books that the source treats as one document in a remark on usage.
shapes.test: A slash whose container is top.

shapes.means: unverified: read here as a stray sign of the source's file after a name, directly before a comma, which does nothing there.
shapes.test: A backslash whose container is top.

shapes.means: unverified: the file's stand-in for capital Ṣ, directly before a letter at about nine in ten of its uses in the record; here, after my Lord Yahweh and before a stop, it shortens the title the record goes on to point to, an abbreviation.
shapes.test: Every occurrence of the U+201A character.

homonyms.reason: The route text carries no entry number. The heading of the source's own record gives 4,828 of its 4,828 entries a BDB number and 4,795 of them a Strong's number (axis: records); the store dropped both, and the route text names neither; two entries under one letters key stand there as separate texts with nothing to tell them apart (example key אדר: its 5 route texts come from 3 entries of the record). keys_with_more_than_one_route_text counts senses and homonyms together. By the audit, in which a text counts as placed in an entry only where no letter stands directly beside it in the record, so that it cannot stand inside a longer word, of the 1,681 such keys (axis: keys; 3,681 letters keys in all) 921 are keys for which one single entry of the record yields every distinct route text of the key, 715 are keys for which no single entry does, so that the texts come from two or more entries that share the letters, true homonyms, and 45 hold a text the audit could not place.

branches.question: Many senses in this dictionary are lists of renderings with commas between them. Lists like crown, wreath (all single words) and wipe, wipe out (all opening with one word) are asked about in B06. When a rendering is a phrase (come near, approach), the route text alone cannot tell a list from a sentence, so the ledger read each such list and kept whole those where it found a piece leaning on another. Lists that open with a small verb and have a later piece that may lean on it are asked about in B02 and B05; one whose later phrases have their own verb (be sorry, have compassion) stays here. Does each comma of these lists divide? The answer holds whatever you answer elsewhere.

options.means: Every comma of these lists cuts, except one between a word and its own plural: the page prints come near and approach as two readings. A word or a phrase prints without the words beside it; nothing is added to it.
No comma of these lists cuts: the page prints come near, approach as one reading, as written.

branches.question: Some lists open with be, and a later word ends in -ed (be accounted, thought, esteemed). Such a word leans on the be: alone it says esteemed, where the source means be esteemed. Does each comma of such a list divide? This answer holds whatever you answer to the other questions.

options.means: Every comma of these lists outside a bracket cuts: the page prints be accounted, thought and esteemed as three readings. A later word in -ed prints without the be it leans on; a later piece with its own verb, as rise in be high, exalted, rise, stands as it is.
No comma of these lists cuts: the page prints be accounted, thought, esteemed as one reading, as written.

branches.question: A few times two renderings have only an exclamation mark, a question mark or a stray full stop between them (lo! behold!). Does that sign divide them into two readings? This answer holds whatever you answer to the other questions.

options.means: The sign between them cuts: the page prints lo and behold! as two readings. The sign at the cut is left out, and a sign at the very end stays.
The sign does not cut: the page prints lo! behold! as one reading, as written.

branches.question: Some lists stand beside a bracket, a quote mark, a cry sign, a grammar word or a short note (produce, furnish: Imperfect), or hold a capital, a piece opened by or, or a part that leans. The ledger read each of them and marked by hand where one rendering ends and the next begins, at a comma, a semicolon or a colon. Does each marked place divide? This answer holds whatever you answer to the other questions.

options.means: Every marked place cuts, beside any cut another answer makes: the page prints produce and furnish: Imperfect as two readings. A sign stays with its own piece, a label at the head stays with the first piece after it, and a tail stays with the last piece before it, even when it speaks of all of them: top, summit, of tree prints top and summit, of tree.
No marked place cuts: the page prints produce, furnish: Imperfect as one reading, as written.

branches.question: Other lists open with a small verb, be, become, grow, have, make or shew, and no later piece is a single form in -ed like esteemed (be firm, fast). Some later pieces still lean on the small verb: alone fast says fast, where the source means be fast; so do broken in be shattered, broken and busied with in be occupied, busied with. Others stand alone (be weak, languish). The ledger did not sort them one by one. Does each comma of such a list divide? This answer holds whatever you answer to the other questions.

options.means: Every comma of these lists cuts: the page prints be firm and fast as two readings, and each later piece prints as the source writes it, without the opening verb, leaning on it where it did. In a few lists only the commas the ledger marked by hand cut: be, or become, far, distant prints be, or become, far and distant.
No comma of these lists cuts: the page prints be firm, fast as one reading, as written.

branches.question: This is the question on words that mostly say the same thing. Some senses in this dictionary are lists of single words or of renderings that open with one word: crown, wreath and wipe, wipe out. In a few others, which the ledger read and listed by hand, a semicolon stands between two groups: prey, food; leaf. Do you want separate pills for such words, or one pill as the source writes it? Today the page prints crown and wreath as two pills, and prey, food and leaf as three. From the day this is wired it prints what you answer here, and one pill until you answer. A word beside its own plural stays together under every answer.

options.means: Separate pills: each comma of these lists and each semicolon of the listed senses cuts, and the page prints crown and wreath as two readings. A semicolon parts its two groups, and this answer cuts no comma inside a group: prey, food; leaf prints prey, food and leaf as two readings. A stop at the very end stays with the last word.
One pill: no comma or semicolon of these cuts, and the page prints crown, wreath as one reading, as the source writes it, and prey, food; leaf as one.

not_done_here: This ledger leaves to the route store which stretch of the source became a route: 3,450 routes (axis: routes) hold no mark at all, so nothing here rules them, among them single grammar words and phrases of a verse that are no readings; and a pointer at the end of a text stays in the last piece, should an answer cut that text; nothing divides at rest here.
